protocol.scope: Conditional clean initial biological-feed operating map: measured native fully developed laminar-branch conductance, source critical-flux comparison under explicit transfer assumptions and actual DWSIM hydraulic recycle. No turbulent, reaction, non-isothermal, fouling-time or indefinitely sustainable-operation prediction. Synthetic channel horizontal, gravity neglected and external permeate pressure uniform; source hydrostatic profiles are not transferred.

biological_feed_extraction.title: Critical flux and rejection behaviour of non-circular-channelled membranes: Influence of some operating conditions
biological_feed_extraction.specimen: Reported non-circular seven-channel ceramic microfiltration family; 0.2 micrometre nominal pore size, not a reconstruction of the project synthetic star
biological_feed_extraction.feed: Effluent of synthetic activated-sludge production system; not the upstream porous-pot recipe in Table 1

measurements.note: Operating-period average and range, not paired point-specific feed measurements or experimental confidence limits

measurements.reported_reproducibility: Section 2.3 states errors never exceed 5%; not identified as a standard deviation, confidence interval or point-specific error bar

transfers_not_measurements: The reported Re 1388 critical flux remains source context. It is not transferred to the project's verified low-Re synthetic star; sustainable flux there remains unavailable.

Reported module-scale rejection is used as a constant local rejection in the distributed tracer calculation; its transfer from 1.6 m/s and 0.1 bar is an assumption. 0.5-0.8 is a chosen scenario sensitivity, not experimental uncertainty.
The module inlet is fixed at the reported average COD. Fresh-feed concentration is derived from the recycle balance, rather than silently held at that same concentration.
A water-carrier property model and a 1.2-times-viscosity scenario are used; neither constitutes measured effluent rheology.

Exploratory high-Re runs and an exploratory 0.8 times 0.95 critical-flux transfer were not accepted for the final low-Re showcase. The final case makes no fouling-free or sustainable-flux admission claim.
biological_feed_extraction.unit_audit: The Markdown omits the micro symbol in some pore-size labels; 0.2 micrometre is established by the microfiltration context and figure axis retained in the supplied source audit. No original PDF typography check is claimed.

evidence.specimen: Seven-channel ceramic microfilter, nominal pore size 0.2 micrometre; star-channel family, not reconstructed geometry.
evidence.protocol: TMP steps 30 min before nonlinearity and 15 min after; average of last time-independent and first time-dependent flux. Maximum TMP 1.2 bar.

reported_reproducibility.interpretation: Authors state errors never exceed 5% for critical flux/rejection; not identified as standard deviation, confidence interval or point-specific uncertainty.

evidence.reading_bounds_scope: Chosen independent +/-2 pixel marker/tick sensitivity, not experimental uncertainty.
evidence.nominal_relation: Piecewise linear interpolation of critical flux versus source Reynolds number; no extrapolation.
evidence.shape_relation: Monotonic brackets without assuming an interpolation shape; exact source nodes use their own reading intervals.
transfer_assumptions: The synthetic hydraulic case is horizontal with gravity neglected and uniform external permeate pressure; no hydrostatic profile is inferred from the vertically mounted source rig.

The hydraulic fixed-impedance anchor derives from the earlier paired Zhu specimen extraction. Chiu uses a different membrane/feed; this combination is a scenario, not a matched experimental prediction.
Transfer the source critical-flux curve to a synthetic wall/support at unchanged nominal selective-layer scenario.
Compare equal Reynolds number and equal channel velocity as separate mappings; neither identifies the source flow convention.
A constant transfer multiplier and capacity fraction are explicit scenario choices, not measured uncertainty.
Apply source module-average Jcrit as a conservative local-flux screen: maximum J(x) <= scenario capacity; this local use is an assumption.
Water-carrier properties; biological feed rheology unavailable. COD retention remains a separate constant scenario.
Changing support geometry is assumed not to change the source critical-flux curve except through local flux redistribution.

geometry.scope: Synthetic axisymmetric connected pore, same necks/interface region, body thickness and representative area; only interior radius changes. Both leads are numerical development sections and excluded from inferred body resistance. No reconstructed experimental specimen.

process.translation: Apply each measured body resistance / measured baseline body resistance to the published 3.12 m/h support impedance. One common baseline calibration; no design-specific fit. Use Zhu PDF-v2 effective non-support impedance and its reading range unchanged across designs. This is a literature-anchored scenario, not an absolute pore reconstruction or a viscosity-corrected experimental prediction.
process.scope: Transmembrane hydraulic-load shaft energy only. Constant inlet properties, linear flow, unchanged effective non-support impedance. Excludes circulation, fouling, osmotic pressure, backwash, motor losses, selectivity and strength certification. Actual DWSIM pump flowsheets; no native membrane separation unit.
